recipes.name: Bread Machine Rolls
ingredients_raw: 1 cup warm water (110 degrees F/45 degrees C)

steps.text: Place bread flour, sugar, salt, milk powder, 1 cup warm water, butter, and yeast into a bread machine in the order listed or follow the order recommended by the manufacturer if different.
Meanwhile, lightly grease a baking sheet.
Remove dough from the machine, deflate, and turn out onto a lightly floured surface.
Divide dough into 12 equal pieces, form into rounds, and place them on the prepared baking sheet.
Cover with a damp cloth; let rise until doubled in size, about 40 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Mix together egg white and 2 tablespoons water in a small bowl; brush lightly onto the tops of risen rolls.
Bake in the preheated oven until rolls are golden brown, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Bread Machine Rolls
raw_recipe.description: These bread machine rolls are tender, squishy, and fluffy with a golden crust and can be served with dinner or used to make delicious sandwiches.

review.reviewBody:
These rolls are tasty and foolproof. Letting them rise the longer amount of time results in a softer, fluffier roll. I skipped the eggwash step to minimize the fuss. The rolls turned out delicious.
I also tried tossing in about a tsp. of dill, oregano and basil at the beginning, then shaping the rolls a little larger for hamburger buns. Again, the recipe turned out delicious.
Note: For bread machine baking, it is IMPERITIVE to measure the flour carefully, by spooning it into a measuring cup and leveling off the top. If you scoop the flour from the bag using the measuring cup itself, the flour compacts and the resulting bread will be dry, dense, or worse.

These were the best rolls that I've ever made and they looked like they came from the bakery! Instead of using powdered milk, I used 1/4 cup of buttermilk and added about 2 tablespoons of extra flour to compensate for the extra liquid. When I let the rolls rise, I covered my pan with saran wrap and placed them in an UN HEATED oven with a bowl of warm water on the rack below them. They turned out excellent! Although you do not need to brush the rolls with the egg mixture, it gives it a a shiny coating, just like the better bakeries, so I recommend that you take the extra 2 min. and use the egg wash on the rolls! Great recipe.

I have made this recipe several times, it's best to put in machine, choose Leven dough. It rises once them I divide the dough and rise once more. Rolls come out out light and airy and absolutely Devine 💯

I used this dough, then rolled it out. Sprinkled shredded cheeses and fresh oregano, then rolled up and cut into buns (cinnamon bun style). Turned out so delicious! I lessened the sugar a little bit when I made the cheese buns.

The only change I made is to replace 1 cup of the bread flour with white whole wheat flour and add 1 teaspoon of Vital Wheat Gluten. This is something that I do with every bread recipe to increase the fiber without changing the taste. On my bread machine, I used the 1 pound setting and that was perfect. I really like these rolls. They're soft and buttery. I put all the leftover rolls into a zipper bag and froze them. Today I took out 2 for dinner and let them thaw on the counter. Delicious!

I took the advice from another poster and used warm milk instead of water and milk powder, but I used almond milk and earth balance for the butter to make this dairy free. I also used 1/2 a tbsp less of sugar than the recipe called for. It rose for an hour in the bread machine and 30 mins outside of it after I punched it down. Best rolls I’ve ever had!

I liked the ease of making these. 5 minutes hands on in the beginning and about 10 at the end of the dough cycle. They came out beautifully golden and fluffy inside. But they were too sweet for dinner rolls. Also, they were too big, almost like a burger bun. I will use less sugar next time and divide the dough into 18 rolls.

These rolls are great. I served them as dinner rolls but they would make great hamburger or sandwich buns as well. I made only a few changes. I reduced the sugar to 2 tablespoons and included the 1 egg white in with the wet ingredients. I also used All Purpose Flour because that was what I had on hand. I brushed the rolls with melted butter both before and right after baking. This ensures a beautiful brown color and also keeps them soft. I sprinkled them lightly with poppy seeds as well after the butter brush and before baking. You could also use sesame seeds, etc. I always put my dough ingredients into the bread machine in the order of wet at the bottom, then all dry ingredients, then yeast on top. Have never been disappointed using that order for dough. It did take my rolls a little longer than 40 minutes, more like an hour to double after coming out of the bread machine. I made 18 smaller rolls which were perfect for dinner. 12 would be a good size for a large sandwich. Thank you for sharing.

Very good and very easy. The rolls were firm on the outside and soft on the inside. Everyone liked them and I will make them again. I made a couple of changes but nothing that changes the integrity of the recipe. To make it healthier I swapped oil for the butter. (butter would taste better) I used 3/4 cup water and 1/4 cup milk instead of the dry milk because I didn't have any dry milk. And because I didn't want to separate out the egg white, I did not use the egg wash at the end I just baked the rolls plain (again the egg would only make the rolls better)

These were super simple and delicious! Very doughy and yummy! I made 3 changes: I didn't have powdered milk on hand, so I just substituted 1 cup of warm milk instead of warm water, and also after reading the reviews saying it was too sweet, I cut down the sugar to 2 tablespoons instead of 3. Also, as some of the other reviewers, I skipped the eggwash step, and the crust was perfect still. These were a hit with all 6 of my family members. We had NO leftovers!

simple and elegant... no fuss or frills. i like the idea of proofing the yeast. 1 min warm water in microwave, dissolve the sugar. add and dissolve the yeast. for a bread machine i adjusted to 15 servings to get a proper loaf
Amazing rolls, need to proof the yeast!!
Easy to do. Used 2 Tbsp oil instead of butter Turned out first time. Lots flavour. Everyone in my family loved So yum
Love them. I substituted 1/4 cup flour with 1/4 cup potato flakes and added 4 tablespoons extra water because potato flakes absorb more water.
I followed the directions precisely and it was so good

These turned out really nice. The dough is wonderful to work with, not sticky at all. I weigh each dough roll to be 53-55 gm which makes about 14 rolls and bake for about 25 minutes. Delish, a keeper. Thanks for the recipe!
